title: GDScript: Use narrowed types from `is` type checks in `if` blocks
body:
When `debug/gdscript/warnings/unsafe_property_access` and `debug/gdscript/warnings/unsafe_method_access` are set to warning or error, accessing a member on a variable that was just checked with `is` still reports the warning, even though the check proves the access is safe:

```gdscript
func foo(reward: Reward) -> void:
	if reward is GoldReward:
		print(reward.value) # UNSAFE_PROPERTY_ACCESS, even though it was just checked.
		print(reward.calc()) # UNSAFE_METHOD_ACCESS.
```

## Approach

The analyzer now tracks a narrowed type for variables that are tested with `is` type tests in the condition of an `if` statement (including the operands of an `and` in that condition):

- While the `true` block of that statement is being resolved, occurrences of the checked variable use the tested type instead of its declared type. Since the narrowed type is a hard type, the member access resolves statically and the unsafe access warnings no longer fire.
- Only local variables, static variables, and function parameters can be narrowed. Identifiers are matched against their source node, so a shadowing declaration in the block (e.g. a `for` loop variable with the same name) is not affected.
- If the variable is assigned inside the block, the narrowed type is invalidated from that point on, since it may then hold a value of another type. Code before the assignment still benefits from the narrowing, matching the execution order.
- This applies to `Variant` variables as well, which is the most common case where the unsafe warnings fire on `is`-checked values.

Completions already partially understand `is` narrowing (see #120492), but this PR makes the analyzer itself aware of it, which is what drives the warnings.

## Tests

- `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/analyzer/features/is_type_narrowing.gd`: reproduces the issue scenario and checks the code both analyzes and runs correctly.
- `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/analyzer/warnings/type_narrowing.gd`: checks that unsafe access warnings are no longer emitted after an `is` check, that they still fire outside the narrowed block, and that an assignment inside the block invalidates the narrowing.

All file-based GDScript tests (512) pass, including the binary tokens variant on Linux CI.
